definitions.explanation: To wear items on the lower body and feet—shoes, pants, skirts, socks. Different from {着|き}る which is for upper body clothing.

examples.japanese: {靴|くつ}を{履|は}いてください。
{今日|きょう}はスカートを{履|は}きます。
{新|あたら}しい{靴|くつ}を{履|は}いている。
{雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は{長|なが}い{靴|くつ}を{履|は}いて、{足|あし}が{濡|ぬ}れないようにしています。
examples.english: On rainy days, I wear tall boots so my feet don't get wet.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}に{行|い}くときは{黒|くろ}い{靴|くつ}を{履|は}きますが、{休|やす}みの{日|ひ}はジーンズを{履|は}いて{白|しろ}い{靴|くつ}で{出|で}かけます。
examples.english: When I go to work, I wear black shoes, but on my days off I wear jeans and go out in white shoes.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). No pair verb. Pattern: Xを{履|は}く (put on X [lower body]).

ASPECT: ている indicates resulting state. {履|は}いている = 'is wearing' (on legs/feet).

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{靴|くつ}を{履|は}く (put on shoes)
・ズボンを{履|は}く (put on pants)
・{靴下|くつした}を{履|は}く (put on socks)
・スカートを{履|は}いている (is wearing skirt)

CLOTHING VERBS: {着|き}る (torso), {履|は}く (legs/feet), かぶる (head). Opposite: {脱|ぬ}ぐ (take off).
